title: March First Movement
summary: On 1 March 1919 Koreans under Japanese rule declared independence in Seoul, where a declaration was read at Tapgol Park while thirty-three leaders signed it at a restaurant and were arrested. Mass, mostly nonviolent protests spread nationwide and met harsh repression; they led to a Korean Provisional Government in Shanghai.

uncertainty.note: The movement began on 1 March 1919; demonstrations continued for months and were suppressed about a year later (sources say this loosely).

as_recorded.value: Began March 1, 1919, and was suppressed about a year later

where.modern_name: Tapgol Park, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea
where.historical_name: Keijo (Gyeongseong), Seoul, Korea under Japanese rule

importance.justification: Nationwide independence uprising against Japanese colonial rule; its aftermath led to the Provisional Government and it is commemorated as a national holiday.

audience_note: Covers the violent suppression of protests, including killings and mass arrests; casualty figures are disputed.

beats.caption: At Tapgol Park in Seoul a student read the independence declaration from the pavilion while the thirty-three leaders signed it elsewhere.
Marchers carried copies home and protests spread nationwide: an estimated two million people in 1,500 to 1,800 demonstrations.
Independence was not won, but the movement led to the Korean Provisional Government in Shanghai and some limited cultural freedoms.

reviewer_note: Casualty totals are left out of the summary because sources disagree; the Korean Culture Project page gives over 7,000 killed, about 16,000 wounded and about 47,000 arrested, and lower Japanese-era counts were not verified on an opened page. The identity of the student who read the declaration is disputed and left unstated. The Provisional Government is given without a day; its April 1919 span is a beat month only. The Korea Culture Project page is a nonprofit newsletter, not scholarship.
